title: Energy stores & transfers
examples: What is the difference between an energy store and an energy transfer?
Can you show me an example of energy moving from one thing to another?
How do I read a Sankey diagram correctly?

explain.say: Today we will learn about where energy is stored and how it moves.

items: Energy can be stored in objects.
Energy moves from one place to another.

explain.say: An energy store is the capacity to do work later.
Energy transfers are when energy moves from one thing to another.
Sankey diagrams show the energy pathways clearly for us.
Consider a simple flashlight working in the dark room.
The most common mistake is forgetting to include all energy losses.

draw.text: Energy Loss: Always account for it

faq.q: What is the difference between an energy store and an energy transfer?
faq.a: An energy store is the capacity to do work later, like stored food energy. An energy transfer is the movement of energy from one thing to another, like burning that food.
asks: Is a battery a store or a transfer?
What is the difference between potential and kinetic energy?

faq.q: Can you give an example of chemical energy being transferred?
faq.a: Burning wood is a good example. The stored chemical energy in the wood transfers into heat and light energy when it burns.
asks: Where does the energy in a matchstick come from?
What is the source of energy in a campfire?

faq.q: How do I read the energy pathways on a Sankey diagram?
faq.a: You follow the width of the bands. The wider the band, the more energy is transferred along that path.
asks: Does the diagram show the total energy?
How do I know which energy type is bigger?

faq.q: Does energy get lost when it changes form?
faq.a: No, energy cannot be created or destroyed. It just changes from one form to another, often as heat.
asks: Does energy disappear when a light bulb glows?

faq.a: It is the energy an object has due to its height in a gravitational field. The higher up it is, the more potential energy it has.
asks: What gives an object potential energy?

facts: Chemical energy is stored in the bonds of chemical compounds.
Gravitational potential energy depends on an object's mass and height.
Kinetic energy is the energy of motion.
In any transfer, the total energy input equals the total energy output.

quiz.why: The band is storing energy due to its stretched shape, which is elastic potential energy.

wrong.1: Kinetic energy is only energy of motion, not stored energy.
wrong.2: Chemical energy comes from bonds, like in food or batteries.
wrong.3: Heat energy is a form of energy, not a stored form.

quiz.say: When a roller coaster car goes down a hill, its energy changes from:
quiz.why: As height decreases, potential energy decreases, and the speed increases, meaning kinetic energy increases.

wrong.0: Heat energy is usually a result, not the starting point of motion.
wrong.2: This would mean the car is slowing down while going higher.
wrong.3: Chemical energy is not the primary source of motion on the hill.

quiz.say: A Sankey diagram shows energy flow from:

options.show: Input Store $\rightarrow$ Useful Output + Wasted Output
options.say: Input Store $\rightarrow$ Useful Output + Wasted Output

quiz.why: The diagram must show the initial stored energy splitting into all resulting forms, including waste.

wrong.0: Ignoring waste energy makes the energy accounting incorrect.
wrong.1: The diagram must show what happens to the energy after the store.
wrong.2: Energy usually transfers into multiple forms, like light and heat.
